content.text: On the deployed teaser: take out the "mit mondjunk az autónál" part, in english too and write there instead "technical facts about the car" or something like that, both in HUngarian. Also, dont employ phrasing that reads like a cheat sheet for a tour guide - it is a teaser for all museum visitor friends. Fix the phrasing in both languages and then deploy the page locally so I can check

input.command: grep -rn -i "mondjunk\|what to say\|talk" lib/app/teaser.js lib/app/i18n/hu.js teaser.html lib/app/viewer.js | head -50

      talk: [
        "Four cylinders of 185 × 200 mm make 21,504 cm³, about 5.4 litres each, for 200 PS at 1,600 rpm.",
        "Benz first built this engine with 15.1 litres for the 1908 racing car. Widening the bore to 185 mm gave 21.5 litres.",
        "Valves in the head, worked by pushrods and rockers from a camshaft low in the block.",
        "At only 1,600 rpm the long stroke still moves each piston at about 10.7 m/s on average, as fast as a 100 mm stroke at 3,200 rpm.",
      ],
      talk: [
        "Bob Burman at Daytona Beach on 23 April 1911: 228.1 km/h over the flying mile, faster than any aeroplane or train of the time. The record stood until 1919.",
        "Barney Oldfield had already reached 211.97 km/h with it there in 1910.",
        "Air drag grows with the square of speed, and the power to overcome it with the cube. Slide the power: doubling it adds only about a quarter more speed.",
        "The wind tunnel shows where that drag comes from. Under Pressure the air piles up red against the radiator; behind the driver's head and the short tail it breaks away into a churning wake, whose low pressure pulls the car back.",
        "Every kilowatt that goes into drag ends up stirring that wake, and the swirls finally warm the air. Watch the readouts: in this slice nearly all the drag is suction behind the car. The push on the radiator is largely cancelled where the air speeds up round its edges, and friction is only a few per cent.",
        "Hence the pointed radiator and the tail cone: the less air the car has to shove aside and the more gently it lets it close up behind, the smaller the wake.",
      ],

      talk: [
        "Rudolf Uhlenhaut's engineers built the 1952 racing 300 SL around a frame of thin welded steel tubes, arranged in triangles so that each tube is only pulled or pushed, never bent. The road car of 1954 kept it.",

        "So the doors are hinged in the roof and open upwards: the Gullwing. Getting in still means climbing over a high, wide sill.",
        "Cut the sides down to a low sill and the same frame twists about three times as much under the same load (in this simple model).",
      ],
      talk: [
        "The M 198 is the 3-litre six of the 300 saloon, reworked: 2,996 cm³, 215 PS (DIN) at 5,800 rpm, 240 hp by the American SAE rating.",
        "A Bosch pump sprays petrol straight into each cylinder during the intake stroke: the first four-stroke production car with petrol direct injection. Watch for the spray.",
        "The engine leans 45° to the left so that the bonnet could sit low. A dry sump, with the oil in a separate tank, keeps the crankcase shallow.",
      ],

      talk: [
        "This is the straight-eight of the W 196 Grand Prix car, enlarged for sports-car racing: 78 mm bore and stroke, 2,982 cc and about 310 PS.",
        "A Bosch pump sprays fuel straight into each cylinder during the intake stroke, watch for the spray. Daimler-Benz knew direct injection from its aero engines.",

      ],
      talk: [
        "At high revs a valve spring can no longer pull the valve back fast enough: the valve floats off the cam and can hit the piston. Raise the speed and watch the spring valve's line leave the dashed cam line.",
        "Mercedes's desmodromic gear has no closing spring. A second cam and a rocker pull the valve shut, so the valve follows the cam exactly at any speed.",
        "The opening and closing cams are matched: their radii always add up to the same value, so the two never fight. Ducati later made the idea famous on motorcycles.",
      ],

content.text:
I've made the changes and the teaser is running locally at **http://localhost:8765/teaser.html**. Use the EN/HU buttons in the top bar to switch language.

**The card you asked about**
- "What to say at the car" is now **"Technical facts about the car"**.
- "Mit mondjunk az autónál" is now **"Műszaki érdekességek az autóról"**. "Érdekességek" (interesting facts) sounded more natural to a visitor than "tények".
- This card is shared with the single-car pages, which friends reach from the teaser's "Open this car…" link. So the new label shows there too, not only on the teaser.

**Other teaser text that read like a guide's notes** (changed in both languages):
- **Header tag:** "Unofficial tour notes" → "A teaser for your visit" / "Kedvcsináló a látogatáshoz".
- **Page title:** "…technical tour: three highlights" → "Under the skin: three cars at the Mercedes-Benz Museum".
- **Intro:** "A taste of the technical tour: three cars…" → "A look under the skin of three cars in the museum…" / "Pillantás a múzeum három autójának karosszériája alá…".
- **Footer:** "Unofficial private tour notes… Rooms and levels follow research notes: confirm on site" → "Unofficial, not affiliated with Mercedes-Benz. Exhibits rotate, so a car may be away when you visit." The teaser doesn't show rooms or levels, so that warning didn't belong there.
- **Link under each car:** "Open this stop on its own page" → "Open this car on its own page".
- **Photo credit line:** "each stop links…" → "each car's page links…".
- **Short description used when the page is added to the Home Screen:** dropped "unofficial technical tour".

I left the three cars' fact lists alone. They are dates, figures and how the parts work. The few direct instructions in them ("Slide the power", "Watch for the spray") tell you what to do with the 3D model, not what to say to a group. The main tour pages (route and single-car pages) keep their tour wording, apart from the shared card label.

**Checks:** `npm test` passes, including the check that every English text has a Hungarian translation. I also loaded the teaser in a headless browser in English and Hungarian: all the new text appears, nothing is missing a translation, and there are no page errors. I didn't run the full iPhone/iPad e2e suite.

Nothing is committed or pushed yet, so the live site hasn't changed. Once you're happy with it locally, tell me and I'll commit and push to main to deploy it.
